generation.entry_policy: every prior historical entry_id must remain present byte-for-byte through its content-addressed identifier
generation.revocation_policy: every prior revocation_id must remain present and a revoked entry_id must never become active again
generation.partition_policy: active and revoked entry IDs are disjoint and exactly partition historical entry IDs
generation.legacy_migration: a verified V1 floor may migrate only by explicit compare-and-swap advance into V2

authority.note: The floor is local anti-rollback custody. It neither admits nor revokes a tuple, creates no compatibility evidence, and authorizes no game effect.

limitations: the floor protects only callers that require and verify it
the floor is not distributed consensus
the floor does not defend against compromise of the owning account or root
revocation prevents future admitted process starts but does not terminate a process that already consumed a valid ticket
relocating the floor requires preserving its exact owner-private custody and content
